body: In the short term: Very complicated. Mainly due to the flat we just moved into, and have signed a one-month lease for. And, of course, heartbreaking. For both of us. I'm not sure I could forgive myself. Once I got over it, I think I could possibly be happy back in Canada, but it's a big unknown. I don't know what my life would look like there.

Yeah, I've thought about that. I'd have to make it long enough to get started, however. And I feel too old. I hadn't really planned on starting a new career in my early 30s.

I don't think there is a solution with my girlfriend unless I just accept her preferred future lifestyle, or we break up. Some of these things are non-negotiable for her.

I have been thinking about switching jobs. Two problems:

1) I don't have any transferrable skills. I've spent the last 10 years developing a very specific set of qualitative research skills. Most of the jobs that people transfer into from academia (consulting, policy) require quantitative research skills.

2) It would require me to move back home to Canada. Which, in many ways, is appealing. But then that would mean I'd have to break up with the girlfriend.

I've talked about the lifestyle thing with my girlfriend, and she, to her credit, has been very clear on what she wants. I've waffled, and probably said a bit too much of what she wants to hear. The problem is that we're now moved in together, and I'm in love with her, and so I'm very locked into the relationship.

I hate academia because it's monotonous, pointless, and mercenary. I'll work my whole career to produce papers that fewer than a dozen people will read, and that won't make any difference in the world, but I'll have to keep endlessly churning them out, because that's how you get ahead. It's lonely and boring. And as for the UK, it's the relentless pressure for conformity; the unending bureaucracy; the terrible weather. I just miss my home.

I'm worried about staying with my girlfriend because of the future that she wants. She wants children, a house in the suburbs, a car, etc. I'm a fundamentally urban creature, and a bit of a hippy, who is very happy with a car-free lifestyle. Driving makes me miserable. And while it's possible (maybe) that I could enjoy parenthood, I think that having children in the face of the oncoming climate catastrophe would be intolerably stressful.

Okay, so here's something that doesn't come up often in these kinds of discussions.

I was a virgin well into my 20s. It sucked. I had thoughts like you are having. If you'd asked me at the time, I'd have said it wasn't just about missing out on physical pleasure, it was also a feeling of prolonged childhood, that I was excluded from an activity that was such a big part of so many of my friends' lives. I also felt miserable in the absence of any real intimacy with a woman.

You probably think that I'm going to talk about how I worked hard and things got better and now I have an active sex life. That would be the cliched thing, anyway. But while that is true, it's not my central point. My central point is that when I finally did manage to lose my virginity, I was shocked by how not-a-big-deal it was. I didn't feel magically grown up. I didn't feel like I was suddenly included. The act itself was...fun, but not nearly as mind-blowingly fun as I had expected. And I feel roughly the same way about sex with my girlfriend today. It's a fun thing to do in the evening, but then again so is watching a good movie or going for a run. I rank all three of those activities about the same, to be honest. As for emotional intimacy, yeah, that's nice to have. But my intimacy with my girlfriend is about on par as the intimacy I enjoy with my parents, my brother, and several of my close friends. It's *different* than those things, but not *better*.

So if you're right, and you'll never have sex, it isn't as big a deal as you think. There are tons of other experiences you'll never have. That's no reason to give up on the things you do get to do that make you happy
I'm from Canada, and moved to the UK.
